judge_assessment.explanation: Every positive claim the judge makes is supported. I recomputed all eight items — 3472→3500, 2961→3000 (carry into the thousands), 4750→4800 at the exact half, 5048→5000 with the place-holding zeros, 4806 < 4860, 3500+3000 = 6500, 4995+10 = 5005, and 2548 to ten/hundred/thousand = 2550/2500/3000 — all correct, and the three manual entries (ids 3, 4, 8) do describe halfway behaviour and the placeholder/carry errors accurately. But the assessment is incomplete on the answer key, which was scored 4. First, the bank row '5. —' is not a manual item: verify.json id 5 is {type: compare, values: ['4806','4860'], order: 'relation', expected: '<'}, a fully verified answer that render_quick_answers._fmt drops because sympify('<') raises. It is the ONLY dash in the bank, sitting beside rows 3, 4 and 8 which DO print numbers even though those are the genuinely manual items — so the one row a grader would read as 'see solution' is the one row that was proved. Second, problem 7 prints 'Then write which places had to change and why', an explanation slot; ids 3, 4 and 8 each carry a manual entry and id 7 carries only the eval 4995+10 = 5005, and the key's item 7 is the one find-and-explain item with no '[Manual review: ...]' bracket. Third, and independent of the judge: the worksheet's own Directions block prints 'Rounding 5,048 to the nearest hundred gives 5,000 — the zeros hold the tens and ones places open', which is the answer to problem 4(b) and most of the answer to 4(a), on the same page, above the problem.

strengths_to_preserve: The misconception traps are declared as the wrong METHOD, not just a wrong number: id 4's trap is {expr: '5000/100', value: 50} which reproduces Ravi's 'counted the hundreds instead of naming the number', and id 7's is {expr: 'n - 90', value: 4905} which reproduces rolling 9 tens to 0 without carrying. verify.py proves each is distinguishable from the right answer, so 'Common wrong answers' is diagnosis rather than decoration.

Problem 8 is the right challenge for this focus: round 2548 to three named places, then explain Kim's 2548 -> 2550 -> 2600 double rounding. It exercises the boundary digit three times at three scales and ends on the one error the whole sheet is about.

The answer key's manual entries carry acceptance criteria a non-specialist can apply — 'credit any sentence naming the tens digit and saying an exact 5 rounds up' and 'credit “the zeros keep each digit in its place”' — rather than a model answer the grader has to match.
Problem 4's key adds a sense check the child can reuse: 'Sense check: 5,048 is close to 5,000, and 50 is nowhere near it.'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds; a relation operator raises and falls back to '---', which is the same glyph the module emits for a manual-only problem. On this sheet the effect is worse than usual because the three genuinely manual items happen to carry numeric siblings, so the only dash in the bank is the one fully verified relation.
evidence: scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt: string branch sympifies, except branch returns '---'; the same '---' is returned by render_entry for a manual-only id.

root_causes.description: The author flagged three of four explanation slots as manual and missed the fourth. Problems 3, 4 and 8 print an explicit '(a) Explain ...' sub-part and each got a manual entry; problem 7 buries its explanation in a trailing clause ('Then write which places had to change and why') and got none. Manual flagging is being driven by the visual shape of the prompt rather than by the presence of an explanation imperative.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 7: 'Write the number that is 10 more than 4,995. Then write which places had to change and why.'
verify.json id 7 holds one entry only: {type: eval, expr: 'n + 10', at: {n: 4995}, expected: 5005} plus a trap. No manual entry.
answer_key.pdf item 7 is the only find-and-explain solution with no '[Manual review: ...]' bracket, where items 3, 4 and 8 all carry one.

root_causes.description: The worksheet's shared Directions block was written by lifting an illustration straight out of the problem set, so it publishes problem 4's answer before the student reaches it. The instructional example and the assessment item use the same number, the same named place and the same result.
evidence: worksheet.pdf Directions, bullet 2: 'A rounded number keeps every place it started with. Rounding 5,048 to the nearest hundred gives 5,000 — the zeros hold the tens and ones places open.'
worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Ravi rounds 5,048 to the nearest hundred ... (a) Explain in one sentence why the rounded number must keep its zeros. (b) Round 5,048 to the nearest hundred correctly.'
study_guide.pdf Skill 3 repeats the same instance: '5,048 to the nearest hundred is 5,000, never 50'.

improvements.title: Print the verified '<' for problem 5 instead of the manual-only em dash
improvements.proposed_change: Handle relation strings in render_quick_answers._fmt before sympify: return '$<$', '$>$', '$=$', '$\le$', '$\ge$', '$\neq$' directly for the corresponding expecteds. Give unrenderable values a marker distinct from the manual '---' so the bank never uses one glyph for 'proved but unprintable' and 'nobody checked this'.
improvements.regression_test: Render curr-104's verify.json and assert the bank line for id 5 is '5.~$<$'. It is '5.~---' today. Add a companion assertion that a manual-only id still renders '---', so the two cases stay distinguishable.
improvements.expected_impact: The only unreadable row of an otherwise complete bank becomes readable, and the compare items on every fraction- and place-value-comparison sheet in the suite stop disappearing.
improvements.risk: Low; formatting-only change to a fallback branch.

improvements.title: Problem 7's 'which places had to change and why' needs a manual entry like problems 3, 4 and 8
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate lint that scans each problem block in the worksheet source for explanation imperatives ('explain', 'why', 'describe', 'say how', 'write one sentence', 'in your own words') and fails the build when the matching verify id has no 'manual' entry. Detection must not depend on the prompt being a lettered sub-part — a trailing clause is the case that slipped here. Add the same rule to SKILL.md's authoring checklist so the JSON is written that way in the first place.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-104's problem 7 text and a verify.json holding only the eval 4995+10 = 5005. The lint must exit non-zero naming problem 7; adding {id: 7, type: 'manual', desc: 'Explain which places changed and why'} must make it pass.
improvements.expected_impact: Brings the manual count on this sheet from 3 to 4 and makes the answer key print a grading note for item 7, matching the treatment its three siblings already get.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning can fire on directions text or on a stem's narrative prose; restrict it to problem bodies and require an explicit acknowledgement rather than a silent suppression.

improvements.title: The Directions block hands the student problem 4's answer (5,048 to the nearest hundred is 5,000)
improvements.proposed_change: Add a consistency lint that collects every (number, named place) or (expression, result) pair appearing in the worksheet's directions/preamble block and fails when a pair matches a problem's own givens and verified answer. Fixing curr-104 means re-illustrating the placeholder rule with a number that appears nowhere in the problem set (e.g. 'Rounding 8,031 to the nearest hundred gives 8,000'). Record the rule in SKILL.md: the directions may state the METHOD and may use an example, but the example's numbers must be disjoint from the problem set's.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose directions contain 'Rounding 5,048 to the nearest hundred gives 5,000' and whose problem 4 verifies estimate('5048', hundred) = 5000. check_prose_consistency.py must exit non-zero naming the collision; changing the directions number to 8,031 must make it pass.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the assessment value of problem 4 on this sheet, and prevents the same lift-the-example-from-the-set shortcut on future sheets, where it is invisible to every existing gate.
improvements.risk: Legitimate overlap exists — a directions example may share a place name or a small integer with a problem — so the lint must match on the full (given, place, result) triple, not on any shared number, or it will be noisy enough to be disabled.

case_summary: A tightly focused misconception sheet whose mathematics is entirely correct and whose traps are declared as reproducible wrong methods rather than bare wrong numbers — the ACCEPT is deserved. Three defects sit under the 31/32 and the judge found none of them. The single em dash in the Quick Answers bank ('5. —') is a fully verified compare '<' dropped by _fmt's bare sympify, and it is uniquely misleading here because the three actual manual items all print numbers. Problem 7's 'write which places had to change and why' is the one explanation slot with no manual entry, so the key gives it no grading note. And the worksheet's Directions block prints 'Rounding 5,048 to the nearest hundred gives 5,000', which is problem 4(b)'s answer and most of 4(a)'s, one page earlier. Preserve the trap encodings, the three-place challenge in problem 8, and the acceptance criteria written into the manual notes.
